name: FOOTPASS-StyleCaptions
description: Soccer video captioning requires descriptions that vary with the target audience and explanatory purpose. However, existing datasets typically provide only single-style captions, overlooking the perspective-dependent nature of match interpretation. To address this limitation, we build a style-conditioned captioning benchmark from the FOOTPASS dataset by annotating each video segment with beginner, tactical, and broadcast-style captions based on structured match information. We further propose a style-conditioned soccer video captioning model that combines learnable style embeddings and style adapters to generate captions according to the specified style. Experiments show that tactical caption generation is more challenging than beginner and broadcast-style captioning, and that fine-tuned vision-language models improve over zero-shot settings but remain below supervised captioning models. Among the evaluated encoders, VideoMAEv2 achieves the strongest overall performance, while the ablation study shows that combining learnable style embeddings, style adapters, and auxiliary losses improves style-conditioned caption generation. These results demonstrate that FOOTPASS-StyleCaptions provides a benchmark for evaluating captioning performance and style controllability across beginner, tactical, and broadcast styles. The dataset, code, prompts, and generation templates will be made publicly available at https://github.com/tamaki-lab/FOOTPASS-StyleCaptions.
